text:
Aisha (CSM): Quick sync — Velocity onboarding SLO acceptance before renewal call next Tue. Need: 1) uptime evidence (last 90 days), 2) p95/p99 latency by production route, 3) proposed credit calc scenarios. Can SRE/ops own the data pulls? :calendar:

Priya (SRE): I can pull uptime & latency. Which window do we want customer-facing — 30 or 90 day rolling? And explicit routes (generate vs embedding)? :thinking_face:

Aisha (CSM): 90-day rolling. Focus on production routes: /generate (text-gen) and /embed. Include tail-latency (p99) and any partial degradations. Customer wants a one-page summary + CSV appendix.

Marco (CS Ops): Will run the exporter. Using scripts/slo_pull.py — will output CSV with daily rows. ETA EOD today. :rocket:

Priya (SRE): Pasting the queries I'll run:
```
-- uptime calc
SELECT service, SUM(available_seconds)/SUM(total_seconds) as uptime
FROM status.buckets
WHERE customer_id = 'velocity' AND ts >= now() - interval '90 days'
GROUP BY service;
```
I'll also get p95/p99 token latency by route and peak-hour slices.

Liam (Enablement): FWIW onboarding checklist shows they still need a runbook review and a short SOC walkthrough. If SLOs are borderline, offering an enablement remediation session is a good safety valve.

Aisha (CSM): Good flag. Marco — can you export daily request counts so I can run credit scenarios (and include error counts)? CSV should be date,route,total_reqs,error_reqs,uptime_frac.

Marco (CS Ops): Yep — will include that and upload to #cs-uploads. Also will tag the March incident with the renewal cohort label.

Priya (SRE): Note: during March incident we failed over to a lower-tier model for ~4h (partial degradation). Should that count toward downtime for credits? Contract language pro-rates partial degradations but want to confirm.

Aisha (CSM): Per contract, partial degradations are pro-rated into uptime calc. I'll loop in legal if anything ambiguous, but assume yes for initial credit calc.

uptime-bot: Incident 2026-03-14-03 closed — 4h partial degradation. Link: https://incidents.redwood/2026-03-14-03

Marco (CS Ops): CSV uploaded: https://files.redwood/velocity-slo/velocity_90d_metrics.csv :link:

Aisha (CSM): Got it, thanks. I'll mock a 2-slide summary + appendix. Sample credit calc I'll use for scenarios:
```
if uptime < 99.9%:
  credit = min( (99.9 - uptime) / 99.9 * monthly_fee, cap )
```
I'll post scenario numbers once I run them against Marco's CSV.

Liam (Enablement): If remediation needed, propose a 90-min technical deep-dive + runbook update. I'll draft an invite and a short outcomes list.

Priya (SRE): Initial numbers (90d): generate p95 = 320ms, p99 = 1.6s; embed p95 = 120ms, p99 = 560ms. I also attached a compact CSV to the upload link.

Aisha (CSM): Those p99s are worth flagging — especially generate at 1.6s. Can we break down by peak hours (8–11am PST)?

Priya (SRE): Yep — adding an hourly slice and will append peak-hour columns to the CSV.

Marco (CS Ops): I'll add label renewal-velocity-march to the incident so it's easy to reference in future renewal packs.

Aisha (CSM): Next steps:
- Priya: final metrics + peak-hour slice by EOD
- Marco: confirm CSV schema upload and incident tag + daily request counts
- Liam: enablement template draft by tomorrow
I'll assemble the customer-facing pack Monday AM and share a draft for review. :handshake:
